text: The fictional class raised $84 for supplies at its book swap.

The fictional Bellwether Campus repair desk tested a new request-intake label during a two-week pilot in three buildings. The label grouped requests into access, equipment, and general questions. Staff kept using the existing form at the same time, so the pilot did not compare response times against the old process.

The desk logged 28 requests: 11 about access, 9 about equipment, and 8 general questions. The pilot ended on May 30. Two requests remained open at that point, and a facilities coordinator said one entry may have been duplicated. The desk has not checked that possible duplicate, so the counts are provisional. The coordinator's name and the date for checking the entry were not included in the summary.

Staff comments were collected informally. The desk did not run a survey, score satisfaction, or compare the comments with another group. The team has not decided whether to keep the label, and no campus-wide rollout is scheduled. The summary suggests discussing the notes at the next internal meeting, but that meeting has no date yet. It also does not assign an owner to the follow-up. The team described the pilot as a way to learn how requests might be grouped; it did not claim that the new labels reduced delays or improved service.
mustPreserve: This was a two-week pilot in three buildings.
The three label groups were access, equipment, and general questions.
The old form remained in use, so response times were not compared against the prior process.
There were 28 logged requests: 11 access, 9 equipment, and 8 general.
